youtube.aciklama: In the Fukuda stepping test, the patient marches fifty steps in place with eyes closed and arms forward. A turn of more than 45 degrees in fifty steps is usually considered abnormal, and the turn is often toward the affected side. But sensitivity and specificity are limited; the test is not used alone to decide the side and is interpreted with other findings.
